title: Hugh Evans, the drummer, and playing at D.H. Holmes
summary: Allen asks about Hugh Evans of D.H. Holmes, who used to play drums. Ridgley recalls his father was good to the band, which played at the store.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Do you know Hugh Evans, he's president of D.H. Holmes' department store now? Mr. Evans? Yeah.
He was the, you mean the old man. No, I mean the one that's living now. The one that used to play drums. Did you ever know him?
Yes, I did know him. Did he ever play with you? Yes, often. Used to come around and play on our job like that. He was a very nice style band.
Harry Sushant told me he took lessons from Chinese, I didn't know that. What did he tell me?
Yeah, maybe he did, but Mr. Evans you're talking about it now since you called it. I had forgotten all about him. His daddy was nice towards our band. We used to play at D.H. Holmes there. Mm-hm.
Mm-hm. He told me he took lessons from Johnny, I didn't know that. He told me, Harry Sushant told me that.

Yeah, maybe he did, because Johnny's always, but Mr. Evans you tell him that now, since you called him, I had forgotten all about him. But he was a very, very fine young fellow, and wherever he'd be. His daddy was nice towards our band. We used to play, it was Jay Day's home then. You know we played one week, we used to go to Jay Day's home, before he opened the stove. And the whole band of us, you know, the drum and everybody, the drummers had a hard time. We used to go all upstairs and everything, all around the stove, every morning. Mr. Evans was a very nice top man. He was at that time, I think he was a son in that charity hospital, the old man was. Very good, because once after that, I'd go to the hospital, I went in and I got a letter. I got a weird sound right away. Very good. That's it.
